info.title: splitforms Form Submission API
info.summary: One HTTPS endpoint that receives HTML, fetch and server-side form submissions.
info.description:
POST any form to `/api/submit` with the form's `access_key`. splitforms validates the request, filters spam with rule-based checks, stores the submission and emails the form owner.

Plans: Free is 500 submissions in total (one-time, no card). Pro is $5/month and Annual is $49/year. Paid plans add signed webhooks, integrations, exports and file uploads.

Rate limit: 6 submissions per minute and 20 per 15 minutes per IP, per form.

Facts checked against the code on 2026-10-02.

externalDocs.description: API reference with cURL, fetch, Python, PHP and Go examples

tags.name: Submissions
tags.description: Send form submissions to a splitforms form.

post.description:
Send the form's `access_key` plus any fields. No Authorization header: the access key identifies the form and is public by design.

The response format follows the request. Requests with `Accept: application/json` or a JSON body, fetch requests, and clients that send no Accept header get JSON. A native HTML form post gets a hosted page, or a redirect when one is configured.

Files need multipart/form-data: up to 5 files of 5 MB each, stored on paid plans with Storage connected. On Free, text fields are saved, files are dropped and the JSON response carries a `note`.

requestBody.description: Accepted content types: application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data, application/json.

200.description: Submission accepted. JSON callers get `{ success: true, message }` plus `redirect`, `redirect_params`, `payment_url`, `note` or `files` when they apply.

302.description: Native HTML post on a form with a redirect URL set in the dashboard. Works on every plan.

303.description: Native HTML post with a valid hidden `redirect` field, or a payment form sending the visitor to Stripe Checkout.

400.description: The request could not be read. `invalid_body`: The body could not be parsed (empty or malformed JSON, or an unreadable form body). `missing_access_key`: No access_key field was sent.

schema.description: Hosted error page, sent to native HTML form posts.

403.description: The form refused the submission. `inactive_form`: The form owner turned the form off. `origin_not_allowed`: Strict origin protection is on and the request came from a domain that is not on the form's allowed list. `form_unavailable`: The form cannot accept submissions.

schema.description: Hosted error page, sent to native HTML form posts.

404.description: Unknown form. `invalid_access_key`: No form has this access_key.

schema.description: Hosted error page, sent to native HTML form posts.

413.description: Request body too large. `payload_too_large`: The body is larger than 5 files of 5 MB plus form fields.

schema.description: Hosted error page, sent to native HTML form posts.

415.description: Unsupported Content-Type. `unsupported_content_type`: The Content-Type is missing or not URL-encoded, multipart or JSON.

schema.description: Hosted error page, sent to native HTML form posts.

429.description: Too many requests or no allowance left. There is no Retry-After header; wait about a minute before retrying a `rate_limited` response. `rate_limited`: More than 6 submissions a minute or 20 per 15 minutes from one IP to one form. `quota_reached`: The account's allowance is used: 500 submissions in total on Free, or the monthly cap on a paid plan.

schema.description: Hosted error page, sent to native HTML form posts.

500.description: Server error. Some 500 responses carry no `code`. `profile_lookup_failed`: The form's account settings could not be read. Retry the request.

schema.description: Hosted error page, sent to native HTML form posts.

options.description: Answers browser preflight requests so the endpoint can be called with fetch from any origin.

access_key.description: The form's public identifier, copied from the dashboard. Safe to embed in client-side HTML; it is not a secret.

subject.description: Subject line of the owner notification email.

replyto.description: Reply-to address on the notification email.

from_name.description: Sender name shown on the notification email.

redirect.description: Thank-you page. Native HTML posts get a 303 to it; JSON callers get it back as `redirect`.

name.description: Name of the person submitting the form.

email.description: Email address of the person submitting the form.

message.description: Message body of the form submission.

botcheck.description: Honeypot field to trap bots; leave empty.

files.description: Array of URLs to uploaded files (paid plans only).
